words: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report of ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, the Prophet explains that obeying rabbis and monks when they make lawful or forbidden things is worship of them.
rows.anchor: للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يا رسول الله ! إنهم لم يكونوا يعبدونهم , قال : أليسوا يحلون لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the People of the Book, whose envy led them to alter scripture, replace stoning with humiliating punishment, follow Satanic material, and reject parts of their book.
rows.anchor: وكما فعلوا في إبدال الرجم في الزنا بالتحميم والجلد ؛ وفي اتباع ما تتلو الشياطين

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines naskh as moving a trace or book from its place by a successor that removes it, or by a substitute that makes its absence unnecessary.
rows.anchor: نقل باد من أثر أو كتاب ونحوه من محله بمعاقب يذهبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is joined without a conjunction because it is tightly connected to what precedes it: God grants this community favor and mercy by changing rulings with circumstances.
rows.anchor: وساقها بغير عطف لشدة التباسها بما قبلها لاختصاصنا لأجل التمشية على حسب المصالح بالفضل والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that the Qurʾān abrogates all earlier religious laws, honoring Muslims with an independent scripture and easing former burdens.
rows.anchor: إن كان المراد نسخ جميع الشرائع الماضية بكتابنا فلما فيه من التشريف بالانفراد بالذكر وعدم التبعية والتخفيف للأحمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse concerns abrogation within the Muslim law, as changing worldly and afterlife interests and causes require.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد نسخ ما شرع لنا فللنظر في المصالح الدنيوية والأخروية بحسب ما حدث من الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An āya may be abrogated by removing its ruling or its recitation after revelation.
rows.anchor: أي فنرفع حكمها , أو تلاوتها بعد إنزالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn ʿĀmir’s reading, the phrase can mean that God commands the abrogating act; the āya may belong to an earlier law, such as the former qibla, or not.
rows.anchor: أو نأمر بذلك على أنها من النسخ على قراءة ابن عامر , سواء كانت في شرع من قبل كاستقبال بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The form suggests that earlier communities sometimes lost a ruling without an equal or better substitute; Muslims should welcome replacement with joy or gratitude for what is better.
rows.anchor: وفي صيغة نفعل إشعار بأن من تقدم ربما نسخ عنهم ما لم يعوضوا به مثلا ولا خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative nunsihā, from ansā and read by readers other than Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, means that God commands leaving the āya unrevealed.
rows.anchor: من أنسى في قراءة غير ابن كثير وأبي عمرو , أي نأمر بترك إنزالها

words: أَوْ نُنسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍۢ مِّنْهَآ أَوْ مِثْلِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing takes immediate abrogation as removal of a ruling or wording, while postponement delays repeal for a time, as with the qibla, before a better or equal replacement comes.
rows.anchor: بأن نؤخر نسخها أو نتركه - على قراءة { ننسها } زمنا ثم ننسخها كالقبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī endorses al-Ḥarālī’s distinction: naskh succeeds and ends an earlier ruling, while nasʾ delays it and can let it return.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : وهو الحق إن شاء الله تعالى . والنسء تأخير عن وقت إلى وقت

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says this subtle distinction escaped most scholars, except the imams from the Prophet’s family, because succession and postponement are easily confused.
rows.anchor: لم يكد يتضح معناه لأكثر العلماء إلا للأئمة من آل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لخفاء الفرقان بين ما شأنه المعاقبة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet temporarily forbade eating sacrificial meat after three days because visitors had arrived from the desert; believers mistook the delay for abrogation until he explained its cause.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى فسره فقال : ( إنما نهيتكم من أجل الدافة )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: A ruling withheld for a cause and restored when that cause disappears is nasʾ; fighting when strong and making truce when weak are examples.
rows.anchor: ومنه المقاتلة للعدو عند وجدان المنة والقوة والمهادنة عند الضعف عن المقاومة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī calls this verse one of the Qurʾān’s comprehensive passages and compares its alternating and recurring rulings to the succession and cycles of seasons.
rows.anchor: فبحق أن هذه الآية من جوامع آي الفرقان , فهذا حكم النسء والإنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī summarizes nasʾ as delaying a permission or prohibition until another time, following Arab usage, and directs readers to the discussion of 9:37.
rows.anchor: وحاصله تأخير الحل كما ذكر أو الحرمة كما في المتعة ونحو ذلك إلى وقت آخر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes divinely caused forgetting from postponement: God may make a prophet forget what is not normally subject to delay, then reveal its instruction as Sunna.
rows.anchor: وأما النسيان والتنسية فمعناه أخفى من النسيء وهو ما يظهره الله من البيانات على سبيل إدخال النسيان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that he forgets in order to establish a Sunna.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن تنسيته كما ورد من قوله : إني لأنسى لأسن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs people to say that they were made to forget, rather than saying simply that they forgot.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام في إفصاح القول فيه : ( بئسما لأحدكم أن يقول : نسيت , بل هو نسي )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī cites the Prophet’s standing after two rakʿas and ending prayer after two as divinely disclosed Sunnas arising through forgetfulness; such prayer is no less than prayer without that lapse.
rows.anchor: ومنه قيامه من اثنتين وسلامه من اثنتين حتى أظهر الله سنة ذلك لأمته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s sleep through a prayer occasioned a second way to determine its time: by remembering it, alongside its ordinary time marked by the sun.
rows.anchor: منامه عن الصلاة حتى أظهر الله توقيت الصلاة بالذكر كما كان قد أظهرها بالوقت الزماني

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: A prayer performed when remembered counts as performance by that measure, while it counts as make-up because its ordinary solar time has passed.
rows.anchor: ولصحة وقوعها للوقتين كانت الموقتة بالذكر أداء بحسبه , قضاء بحسب فوت الوقت الزماني

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The community benefits from repeal, postponement, and divinely caused forgetting; the later instruction is better in its effect, and the process serves the community through its changing conditions.
rows.anchor: وفي كل ذلك إنباء بأن ما وقع من الأمر بعد هذا النسيان خير من موقع ذلك الأمر

words: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ability to provide the promised replacement proves his complete power, which entails knowledge; unlike human rulers, he need not fear subjects’ reaction to changing a command.
rows.anchor: والقدرة الشاملة التامة مستلزمة للعلم أي وليس هو كغيره من الملوك إذا أمر بشيء خاف غائلة أتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī frames rejection of divine abrogation as a major error of the People of the Book, despite the burdens removed by the new scripture and their own alteration of earlier law.
rows.anchor: ولا سيما ما فيها من الآصار والأغلال أشار سبحانه إلى أن من أعظم ضلالهم وغيهم ومحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book object that God cannot abrogate, although they themselves permit scriptural distortion; this inconsistency leads them to reject any messenger whose teaching they dislike.
rows.anchor: مما هو موجود في كتابهم كما أمر آنفا , ومما سوغوه لأنفسهم بالتحريف والتبديل , ولزم من ذلك تكذيب كل رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection says an omniscient God would not command something and later forbid it, since he would already know whether it was beneficial or harmful.
rows.anchor: وأنه لو كان من عند الله لما تغير لأنه عالم بالعواقب , ولا يخلو إما أن يعلم أن الأمر بذلك الشيء مصلحة

words: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī answers that God creates circumstances that make a ruling beneficial at one time and harmful at another, according to wisdom and purposes governing the world’s finite course.
rows.anchor: فيخلق بقدرته من الأسباب ما يصير الشيء في وقت مصلحة وفي وقت آخر مفسدة لحكم ومصالح دبرها

words: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited scripture says that God is not questioned about what he does, supporting his freedom to legislate as he wills.
rows.anchor: مما هو موجود في كتابهم كما أمر آنفا , ومما سوغوه لأنفسهم بالتحريف والتبديل

words: ولو شاء ربك لأمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have made everyone believe and made humanity one community, but instead governs as sovereign over the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء ربك لأمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا

words: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership of heaven and earth means he acts in their substances and states as he wills; a servant cannot object to the sovereign master, who owes no one a ruling fitted to that person’s preferences.
rows.anchor: ولكنه مالك الملك وملك السماوات والأرض , يتصرف على حسب ما يريد

words: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī links the two proofs: by being able over all things God divides or specifies revelations, and by owning heaven and earth he orders affairs.
rows.anchor: فهو بما هو على كل شيء قدير يفصل الآيات , وهو بما له ملك السماوات والأرض يدبر الأمر

words: وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِن وَلِيٍّ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses wilāya as taking charge of an affair through a connecting bond.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهي القيام بالأمر عن وصلة واصلة

words: وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِن وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having no protector or helper besides God urges believers to turn wholly to him and warns those not yet fully faithful against resisting a later ruling as the Jews did.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك تعريض بالتحذير للذين آمنوا ولم يبلغوا درجة المؤمنين من مخالفة أمره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees this address as a comprehensive frame for the later changes in detailed rulings and conditions, like the earlier address introducing parables at the sūra’s opening.
rows.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة خطاب جامع لتفصيل ما يرد من النسخ في تفاصيل الأحكام والأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm asks for a community submitted to God in which its members can lead one another; the passage also cites Joseph’s prayer at 12:101.
rows.anchor: طلب بقوله : { أمة مسلمة لك } أن يكونوا بحيث يؤم بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a Muslim needs knowledge, Ibrāhīm asks God to show them their rites; the direct divine teaching of pilgrimage marks its special honor.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المسلم مضطرا إلى العلم قال : { وأرنا مناسكنا } وفي ذلك ظهور لشرف عمل الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrimage is a sign of the coming Day of Judgment, when there will be no intermediary between Lord and servants.
rows.anchor: لكونه علما على آتي يوم الدين حيث لا واسطة هناك بين الرب والعباد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī derives mansak from n-s-k and defines it as an act performed in devotion and religious observance.
rows.anchor: والمنسك مفعل من النسك وهو ما يفعل قربة وتدينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human incapacity makes divine enabling necessary; asking forgiveness after a good deed reflects the knowers’ return of their works to the Creator.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان محل العجز فهو أضر شيء إلى التوفيق قال : { وتب علينا } إنباء بمطلب التوبة أثر الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s habit is generosity: al-Tawwāb returns servants to safety after their enemy has led them astray, displaying his favor and power; al-Raḥīm further explains this hope.
rows.anchor: أي الرجاع بعباده إلى موطن النجاة من حضرته بعد ما سلط عليهم عدوهم بغوايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having asked for direct instruction for himself, Ibrāhīm asks that his descendants receive it through the customary intermediary of a messenger.
rows.anchor: ولما طلب ما هو له في منصب النبوة من تعليم الله له المناسك بغير واسطة طلب لذريته مثل ذلك بواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community among whom the messenger is raised consists of the submitted people descended from Ibrāhīm and his son Ismāʿīl.
rows.anchor: أي الأمة المسلمة التي من ذريتي وذرية ابني إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is Muḥammad, the only descendant of Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl sent with a Book; being one of them makes him more compassionate and easier to follow and support.
rows.anchor: وذلك الرسول هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم , فإنه لم يبعث من ذريتهما بالكتاب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer is Ibrāhīm’s, the father of the Arabs and noblest of his descendants; the People of the Book are censured for hostility toward the messenger sent to purify them through guidance.
rows.anchor: فهو دعوة إبراهيم عليه السلام أبي العرب وأكرم ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger recites by reading the signs continuously and in sequence.
rows.anchor: يتلوا } أي يقرأ متابعا مواصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs are indicators of him, whether revealed in scripture or inferred from it.
rows.anchor: أي علاماتك الدالات عليك أعم من أن يكون نزل بها الكتاب أو استنبطت منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is complete and comprehensive of every scripture; Biqāʿī evokes the expression that Muḥammad was given comprehensive speech.
rows.anchor: الكتاب } الكامل الشامل لكل كتاب ( أوتيت جوامع الكلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom comprises every command prescribed for them, protecting their worldly and afterlife paths from deviation and ruin.
rows.anchor: وهي كل أمر يشرعه لهم فيحفظهم في صراطي معاشهم ومعادهم من الزيغ المؤدي إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification comes after teaching because Islam already provides its foundation, while this community has greater need for instruction.
rows.anchor: فإن أصلها موجود بالإسلام فأخر قوله : { ويزكيهم } أي يطهر قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Sūrat al-Jumuʿa, purification precedes teaching because the general unlettered audience first needed release from major shirk to receive knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه في سورة الجمعة بعثه في الأميين عامة اقتضى المقام تقديم التزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Āl ʿImrān, purification comes first for believers because attachment to worldly spoils caused defeat and is the source of defilement.
rows.anchor: وأما تقديمها في آل عمران مع ذكر البعث للمؤمنين فلاقتضاء الحال بالمعاتبة على الإقبال على الغنائم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines al-ʿAzīz as the one who overcomes everything and is overcome by none, and al-Ḥakīm as one whose intended act cannot be undone.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يغلب كل شيء ولا يغالبه شيء , لأن العزة كما قال الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge and purified character require arduous struggle and divine ordering; these qualities are especially necessary for a messenger, whose enemies God defeats and whose affairs none can overturn.
rows.anchor: فكيف بما يصلح منه للرسالة ؟ وفيه إشارة إلى أنه يكبت أعداء الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next question follows from the messenger’s divine qualities: only one who debases himself would turn away from Ibrāhīm’s upright, pure, compassionate way.
rows.anchor: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم } المستقيم الطريقة , الطاهر الخليقة , الشفيق على ذريته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines safāha as lightness of judgment where firmness is expected; Biqāʿī says the one who rejects Ibrāhīm thereby insults and devalues himself.
rows.anchor: والسفاهة خفة الرأي في مقابلة ما يراد منه من المتانة والقوة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the accusative nafsahu makes folly encompass the whole person and shows it originating within the self.
rows.anchor: وفي نصب النفس إنباء بلحاق السفاهة بكلية ذي النفس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī treats the self as the source through which evil arises, whereas God gives good directly or indirectly, making the self’s role a proof against people.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعالى يعطي الخير بواسطة وبغير واسطة , ولا يحذى الشر إلا بواسطة نفس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says Ibrāhīm’s way is evident in reason and experience, so no one has an excuse for abandoning it.
rows.anchor: لظهور شاهدها في العقل وعظيم بركتها في التجربة , لأن من ألقى بيده لم يؤاخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisāṣ means killing a killer for the person killed, without excess or aggression; it preserves life because people who know they will be killed refrain from killing.
rows.anchor: هذا الجنس وهو قتل النفس القاتلة بالنفس المقتولة من غير مجاوزة ولا عدوان

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees worldly life preserved for the killer’s kin who might otherwise face retaliation, and afterlife life for the offender whose sin is expiated; one under punishment is neither living nor dead in experience.
rows.anchor: فالحياة لمن سوى الجاني من عشيرته ممن كان يعتدى عليه بجناية غيره في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī rejects the pre-Islamic maxim that killing most effectively suppresses killing: expecting only one execution for two deaths can encourage murder and retaliation.
rows.anchor: لأن من علموا أنهم إذا قتلوا اثنين لا يقتل بهما إلا واحد ربما كان ذلك مجريا لهم على القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic wording exceeds the Arab maxim in meaning while using fewer letters; attempts to clarify the maxim add length without matching its fluency or sweetness.
rows.anchor: بينها وبين ما في القرآن كما بين الله وخلقه فإنها زائدة على عبارة القرآن في الحروف وناقصة في المعنى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī calls the albāb the inner core of reason, which notices God’s command in visible things, while outward reason notices created realities.
rows.anchor: وهو باطن العقل الذي شأنه أن يلحظ أمر الله في المشهودات كما شأن ظاهر العقل أن يلحظ الحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compliance with the law brings taqwā and restrains killing; al-Ḥarālī reads laʿalla as leaving room for different outcomes, including greater aggression in some.
rows.anchor: أي الله بالانقياد لما شرع فتتحامون القتل

words: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After urging the giving of wealth and then life through retaliation, the passage urges bequest of wealth near death, when worldly poverty is no longer feared and afterlife reward is hoped for.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك بذله في حال الإشراف على النقلة والأمن من فقر الدنيا والرجاء لغنى الآخرة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī connects the sequence to graded spiritual education: the preceding passages address those hoping to attain taqwā, then raise the address to what is due of the already pious; the mention of death in retaliation leads to bequest at death.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في الخطاب السابق ذكر القتل والقصاص الذي هو حال حضرة الموت انتظم به ذكر الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bequest was initially obligatory, as the emphatic phrase indicates, then inheritance rules abrogated that duty for inheriting relatives while leaving bequest permissible in other cases.
rows.anchor: ثم نسخ بآية المواريث وجوبه فبقي جوازه , وبينت السنة أن الإرث والوصية لا يجتمعان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that God assigned each right-holder their due and that there is no bequest for an heir; Aḥmad and the four collections transmit it from ʿAmr b. Khārija and Abū Umāma.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إن الله سبحانه وتعالى أعطى كل ذي حق حقه فلا وصية لوارث ) رواه أحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death’s arrival means the approach of its causes and signs.
rows.anchor: أي بحضور أسبابه وعلاماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr here is property that can be bequeathed, whether little or much; Biqāʿī cites 28:24 as an example of the word for a small amount.
rows.anchor: أي ما لا ينبغي أن يوصى فيه قليلا كان أو كثيرا , أما إطلاقه على الكثير فكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents are named first because of their honor and the magnitude of their right.
rows.anchor: بدأ بهما لشرفهما وعظم حقهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bequests to other close relatives must follow recognized fairness, with just distribution according to what people know as equitable.
rows.anchor: أي العدل الذي يتعارفه الناس في التسوية والتفضيل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines maʿrūf as what people’s souls accept without aversion.
rows.anchor: والمعروف ما تقبله الأنفس ولا تجد منه تكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis in ḥaqqan and ʿalā al-muttaqīn stirs hearers to obey and reminds them of their coming account before God.
rows.anchor: وأكد الوجوب بقوله : { حقا } وكذا قوله : { على المتقين * } فهو إلهاب وتهييج وتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing a lawful bequest includes replacing its designated item when specific or reducing its amount when fungible.
rows.anchor: بأن غير عينه إن كان عينيا أو نقصه إن كان مثليا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī infers that fixed inheritance shares answered failures in bequest: two thirds were assigned by share law, the remaining third kept the prior rule, and fixed shares replace bequests to heirs.
rows.anchor: فلما فرضت الفرائض اختزل من يديه الثلثان وبقي الثلث على الحكم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changer is culpable after learning the bequest with certainty; one who lacks certainty but makes a sincere legal judgment bears no sin.
rows.anchor: أي علمه علما لا شك فيه , أما إذا لم يتحقق فاجتهد فلا إثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responsibility for the alteration falls on those who change the will, by action or implication, rather than on the person who made it.
rows.anchor: أي التبديل { على الذين يبدلونه } بالفعل أو التقدير لا يلحق الموصى منه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears both parties’ statements and knows their hidden and public intentions, warning against concealed wrongdoing and unjust supplication.
rows.anchor: أي لما يقوله كل منهما { عليم * } بسره وعلنه في ذلك

words: فَمَنْ خَافَ مِن مُّوصٍۢ جَنَفًا أَوْ إِثْمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawf here includes knowing, expecting, or supposing an injustice, indicating that a reasoned suspicion can suffice.
rows.anchor: أي علم وتوقع وظن , أطلقه عليه لأنه من أسبابه , ولعله عبر بذلك إشارة إلى أنه يقنع فيه بالظن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes accidental inclination in a will as janf from deliberate injustice as ithm; al-Ḥarālī describes janf as hidden oppression disguised as piety.
rows.anchor: وكان حقيقة معنى الجنف إخفاء حيف في صورة بر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before death, reform means advising the testator toward a mutually agreeable will; after death, it means reconciling beneficiaries and heirs to prevent conflict.
rows.anchor: أي بين الموصي والموصي لهم إن كان ذلك قبل موته بأن أشار عليه بما طابت به الخواطر
